messages:
alex: started a bulk BMC flash across ap-se3 edge racks 7-12, noticed a bunch of IPMI session timeouts and ARP churn. some GPU nodes failing provision, appears tied to oob mgmt plane. thoughts? :confused:
mira: saw that. noisy ARP on vlan 420 around 12:14 UTC. ACL hit counters climbing on the jumphosts.
infra-oncall: paging infra-oncall. I rolled the flash job for rack-9 back to previous image at 12:17 to stop the churn.
ajonah: can you paste the error from the flasher? I want to check if secureboot flags flipped during write.
alex: logs from the job (trimmed):
```
[12:12:03] flashing bmc bmc-apse3-rack10-node02.bin
[12:12:35] ipmi_session_open: timeout after 30s
[12:12:35] arp: gratuitous failed, dev=eth1
[12:12:36] secureboot: current=1 expected=1
[12:12:36] write: checksum ok
[12:12:37] bmc reboot pending
[12:13:05] ipmi_session_open: timeout after 30s
[12:13:06] provisioning: gpu attach failed: timeout waiting for console
```
mira: interesting that secureboot reported current=1 expected=1, so not an obvious toggle but the IPMI layer is flapping. could be watchdog resets during flash.
pm-lina: flagging this since some customer jobs hit errors. any risk to VM/tenant isolation?
infra-oncall: no evidence of NVMe or host disk corruption. just the oob plane being noisy. my guess is burst of ARP + ACLs causing the BMC management network to drop sessions and the flasher to retry aggressively, which leaves some nodes in partial state.
ajonah: repro steps I ran in staging: single node flash -> fine. concurrent flashing of 8 nodes on same OOB vlan -> saw arp storms and a couple of IPMI resets. looks like the flasher's multicast/announce floods the switch TCAM.
alex: switch counters on oob-switch-3 show mc/bcast queue rise then ACL hit increments. need to throttle the flasher concurrency or fix ACL behavior.
infrastructure suggestion: add 1s jitter + limit to 2 concurrent flashes per rack, and rate-limit gratuitous ARP.
pm-lina: how soon can we patch the flasher? customers waiting on capacity.
infra-oncall: quick mitigation: pausing job, draining nodes that are partially provisioned, and requeue with concurrency=2. doing that now.
sre-bot: Incident created: INC-2026 - AP-SE3 OOB flash storm. Priority: P2. Assigned: eng-infra.
mira: also found ephemeral ARP entries not aging due to switch firmware bug. there is a vendor patch but it needs maintenance window.
ajonah: for now, we should avoid running fleet-wide flashes that induce broadcast storms. propose: 1) immediate: requeue with concurrency=2 and add 1-2s jitter 2) short-term: patch flasher to use unicast IPMI where possible or stagger by rack 3) mid-term: vendor switch FW or config change to fix ARP aging and increase TCAM for ACLs.
alex: agree. I'll open a PR to add jitter and a throttle flag on the flasher with default 2.
pm-lina: please share ETA for PR and a rollback runbook for nodes that are partially flashed. customers want timeline.
alex: PR draft in a few hours, will roll to staging tonight. rollback runbook: 1) isolate node on maintenance vlan 2) use serial console to check firmware state 3) if BMC responsive, re-flash last-known-good; else mark for manual reprovision. I'll paste precise steps after PR.
mira: marking racks 7-12 paused in the provisioner.
infra-oncall: mitigation actions done: paused bulk job, requeued 8 stuck nodes to manual queue, lowered concurrency cluster-wide.
sre-bot: Update INC-2026: Mitigation applied. Monitoring ARP/cpu on oob-switch-3 and BMC session success rate.
ajonah: one more note — we saw a secureboot corollary on 2 nodes where UEFI vars reported 'rollback required' after a partial flash. I'm adding a check to the flasher to validate UEFI vars post-flash and auto-trigger rollback flash of bootrom if mismatch.
alex: good catch. add that to the PR. also ensure alerts trigger when secureboot flag != expected for >5 mins.
pm-lina: thx team. I'll update affected customers and include mitigations and ETA to patch. :thumbsup:
infra-oncall: logging follow-up: saved pcap of ARP flood to s3://redwood-debug/ap-se3/3959876543-arp-pcap.pcap
mira: will coordinate vendor ticket for switch FW tomorrow.
alex: reopening flash job only after we validate jitter/throttle and one successful canary rack.
jonah: will own the canary and runbook checks. ping me when ready.
pm-lina: keeping this on customer watchlist.
infra-oncall: leaving the thread open for postmortem notes.
